summary:
MissionForge is an interactive 2.5D space mission simulation game developed to make space exploration and mission design accessible, engaging, and educational. Inspired by real NASA missions, it allows players to design rockets, assemble spacecraft, launch missions, control flight stages, deploy satellites, and explore planetary destinations through an interactive simulation experience.

MissionForge addresses the challenge of making complex space mission concepts understandable through hands-on experimentation rather than passive learning. By combining rocket construction, flight simulation, mission objectives, resource management, and a visually engaging space environment, it transforms abstract aerospace concepts into an interactive experience.

The project aims to bridge the gap between space science and interactive learning, encouraging curiosity, engineering thinking, and exploration. MissionForge demonstrates how game-based simulation can introduce students and enthusiasts to the challenges of real-world space missions while making space exploration more approachable and enjoyable.
details:
MissionForge: Bringing Space Exploration to Life

Overview

MissionForge is an interactive 2.5D space mission simulation game inspired by real-world NASA missions. It transforms complex aerospace concepts into an engaging, hands-on experience where users can design rockets, assemble spacecraft, launch missions, control flight stages, deploy payloads, and explore planetary destinations.

How It Works

MissionForge combines a vehicle construction workshop, a flight simulation environment, and a mission progression system. Players assemble rockets using different components, configure their vehicles, and launch them into simulated space environments. The simulation incorporates concepts such as gravity, thrust, velocity, fuel consumption, staging, orbital mechanics, and mission objectives to introduce the challenges of spaceflight.

The project also incorporates mission-inspired experiences based on real space exploration initiatives, connecting interactive gameplay with scientific curiosity.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Space exploration can be difficult to understand through textbooks or static presentations alone. MissionForge makes these concepts more approachable through interactive experimentation. It encourages engineering thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and curiosity about aerospace science. Our intended impact is to make space exploration more accessible to students and enthusiasts while demonstrating the educational potential of simulation-based learning.

Technology and Development

MissionForge was developed using Python for backend simulation and mission systems, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend and interactive gameplay. The project uses a modular architecture separating simulation logic, vehicle systems, mission data, and user interface components. Development and testing were carried out using tools such as Visual Studio Code and browser-based testing workflows.

Creativity and Design Considerations

Our creative approach combines the accessibility of a game with the concepts of an aerospace engineering simulator. We chose a 2.5D presentation to balance visual engagement, performance, and development feasibility. The team considered usability, simulation clarity, realistic mission concepts, resource management, and accessibility when designing the experience.

MissionForge demonstrates how interactive technology can turn the complexity of space exploration into an experience that inspires learning, experimentation, and discovery.
